name: flag_phoneme_boundary_bits
description: Walks two parallel phoneme tables in the device data, setting the boundary flag bits on each entry that opens or closes a phoneme group, and stops at the end-of-list marker. It calls one helper routine for the transition checks.

name: flag_phoneme_sequence_edges
description: Starts from a phoneme index and a flag table pointer, sets the same boundary flags while scanning the sequence, and returns at the end-of-list marker. It calls three helper routines for transitions it cannot resolve inline.

name: scan_phoneme_run_flags
description: Scans runs of phoneme codes and sets the group-start and group-end bits in the flag table at each transition, jumping back into the boundary loop when a flag bit is set. It calls one helper and returns at the end marker.

name: mark_phoneme_run_ends
description: Advances through a phoneme list and sets the end-of-run and continuation bits in the flag table where a code's class bits match, looping until the terminator. It calls one helper routine.

name: mark_phoneme_run_stops
description: Walks a phoneme run and sets the stop flag on its last flagged entry, with a second flag on the entry before it, and repeats until the terminator. It calls one helper routine.

name: set_phoneme_run_flags
description: Sets the first two flag bits on the entries around each boundary, then continues scanning and sets the closing bit on the last flagged entry. It returns at the end-of-list marker.

name: fill_period_records_from_table
description: Divides a fixed clock constant by a stored period value to get a base rate, then writes scaled rates into 8-byte-spaced records for each active phoneme, interpolating between three stored points when a mode flag is not set. It returns after writing the final terminator record.

name: render_keyframe_segments
description: Writes interpolated rate values across a segment defined by three per-point values, placing intermediate records by the ratio of their differences, and stops at the end-of-list marker. It calls two helper routines.

name: fill_segment_rates_until_end
description: Repeats the segment interpolation over successive phoneme entries and writes the final rate into the last record before returning at the end-of-list marker. It calls one helper routine.

name: emit_interpolated_segment_rates
description: Reads per-phoneme segment codes, converts each into a base rate with a division, and writes interpolated values into the output records until the terminator. It calls one helper routine.

name: step_segment_rate_interpolation
description: Steps through a segment and writes interpolated rates into the output records, using the ratio of the segment's two point values to place each value. It calls two helper routines.

name: accumulate_and_emit_segment_rates
description: Accumulates the widths of consecutive segment entries and writes the interpolated rate at each segment boundary, then places the final value after the last segment. It calls one helper routine.

name: fill_fixed_period_records
description: Writes a fixed-rate value, the base rate divided by a constant, into every 8-byte-spaced output record until the terminator is reached.

name: stub_empty_return
description: Consists only of a return instruction, so it performs no work and has no behaviour beyond returning to its caller.

name: compute_frame_rate_values
description: Walks the phoneme frame list and chooses a 6-bit rate value for each frame from a per-phoneme lookup table, adjusted by flag bits and clamped to 63. It keeps the top two bits of each destination byte and calls a helper for each adjustment.

name: compute_frame_rates_from_codes
description: Computes a 6-bit rate value for each frame from the phoneme code and the neighbouring codes, using a lookup table and flag-driven adjustments, with the result clamped to 63. It calls three helper routines.

name: scale_frame_rate_values
description: Scales the lookup-table rate for each frame by a stored ratio and adds a small offset when a flag bit is set, clamping the result to 63. It writes the frame value into the destination table and calls helpers for the neighbour checks.

name: scale_frame_rate_codes
description: Recomputes the 6-bit frame rate for each phoneme code from its neighbours' flag bits and a lookup table, writing each result to the destination and clamping at 63. It calls three helper routines.

name: rescale_frame_rate_tail
description: Finishes the frame-rate pass for the last phoneme group, reusing the neighbour checks and the scaled lookup value, and returns at the end-of-list marker. It calls three helper routines.

name: rescale_frame_rate_pass
description: Repeats the frame-rate scaling across the phoneme list, writing a clamped 6-bit value per frame and looping until the end marker. It calls several helper routines for the neighbour adjustments.

name: rescale_frame_rate_entries
description: Walks the phoneme list writing a clamped 6-bit rate for each entry, choosing the lookup value from the neighbouring codes and their flags, and returns at the end-of-list marker. It calls several helper routines for the neighbour adjustments.

name: rescale_frame_rate_stepping
description: Repeats the frame-rate scaling for each phoneme step, adjusting the rate by neighbour flags and clamping it to 63 before writing it out. It returns when the end marker is reached.

name: rescale_frame_rate_runs
description: Scales frame rates across runs of phoneme codes, switching between the run-continuation and run-start rules, and writes each clamped result into the destination table. It calls three helper routines.

name: rescale_frame_rate_pairs
description: Processes pairs of neighbouring phoneme codes to set the frame-rate values, including a carried-over value from the previous entry, and returns at the end marker. It calls three helper routines.

name: rescale_frame_rate_sequence
description: Steps through a phoneme sequence scaling the frame rate of each entry from its neighbours' flags, and stops when a code without a continuation flag is reached. It calls two helper routines.

name: rescale_frame_rate_scan
description: Scans the phoneme list and rescales the frame rate of each entry that continues a run, returning once the flag sequence ends. It calls two helper routines.

name: compute_scaled_shifted_product
description: Multiplies the low word of one input by a second 16-bit input, then returns a value built from the high word of that product and the low word after adding a constant and shifting right by five bits. It is called from eight places and keeps no state.

name: initialize_and_clear_buffers
description: Stores pointers to fixed offsets in the device state block, advances three of them by two bytes, and clears several 16-bit state fields. It then zeroes six arrays of 32 long words and two more arrays of the same length.

name: advance_counter_and_dispatch
description: Increments a 16-bit counter in the device state and calls a helper on every pass, calling it four more times unless the counter wrapped to zero or overflowed. It returns after those calls.

name: build_phoneme_value_buffer
description: Walks the phoneme code list and its flag list, writing a 4-bit value with a marker bit into the output buffer for each code, and records the counts and first marked position in the state fields. It stops at the end marker or after 128 entries.

name: fill_phoneme_value_table
description: Writes a combined value for each phoneme entry into the table, applies the flag bits of the current and next entries, and updates the counters in the state fields. It returns at the end marker or after 128 entries.

name: expand_phoneme_value_runs
description: Writes one combined value per run of phoneme entries, repeating while the continuation flag is set, and returns at the end marker or after 128 entries.

name: set_flag_and_store_indices
description: Sets the closing bit on the byte at the current table position, then stores the current index and, when the counter is zero, the same index in a second state field. It returns immediately afterwards.

name: resolve_phoneme_flag_runs
description: Marks special phoneme codes in a flag table, then walks backward through the table setting and moving flag bits along each run until the start is reached. It returns once the flag pass completes.

name: resolve_phoneme_flag_chain
description: Resolves the same run-based flag markers as its neighbour, with the state kept in registers, and writes the updated flags back to the table before returning. It calls three helper routines.

name: resolve_phoneme_flag_runs_tail
description: Finishes the backward flag pass for the final phoneme run, applying the closing marker and writing the state pointers back before returning. It calls one helper routine.

name: propagate_phoneme_flag_backward
description: Stores three pointer state values one step back, then walks backward through the flag table setting the marker bit on entries whose codes match and shifting flags along each run. It returns when the index is exhausted.

name: carry_phoneme_flags_backward
description: Walks backward from a starting index over the flag table, ORing the carried flag into each entry and moving or clearing flags on runs where the code matches, until the index reaches the start. It calls two helper routines.

name: merge_phoneme_flag_runs
description: Walks a phoneme flag run from a starting index, moving the code value along matching entries and clearing the source, and resets the run when the index leaves the table bounds. It returns once the start index is exhausted.

name: move_phoneme_code_and_clear
description: Copies the code value from the starting index into the current entry, clears the source when the two positions differ, and carries the flag bit backward through the table along runs of matching codes until the start is reached.

name: set_flag_bit_down_range
description: Sets the lowest flag bit on every entry of a table from the current index down to the first entry.

name: set_flag_bit_run_down
description: Sets the lowest flag bit on each entry of a table from the given index downward to the start of the table.

name: or_mask_back_until_boundary
description: Chooses a mask from the control byte at the previous position, ORs it into table entries walking backward from the current index, and stops early when the companion table marks a boundary.

name: set_mask_and_mark_boundary
description: When the control byte is neither of two special values, ORs a mask selected by a second table into the entry at the current index. If a counter is non-zero it scans backward for a marked entry and sets a fixed low-nibble pattern there.

name: accumulate_table_entries
description: Reads a 16-bit state value and, unless a mode flag is set, runs a few helper calls first, then adds that value to each of eight consecutive 32-bit entries in the state block.

name: compute_clamped_rate_byte
description: Computes a value from a frame index and a rate word, clamps it to a floor of 125 and a ceiling of 165, and stores it as a byte in the output table at the current index.

name: clamp_value_and_store_char
description: Clamps a 16-bit input to a floor of 125 and a ceiling of 165 and stores the result as a byte at the current table position.

name: adjust_output_values_by_flags
description: Computes an interpolation step from the input value and the segment count, then applies scaled adjustments to the output buffer at flagged positions, moving forward and backward from the marked start. It finishes with a final correction pass.

name: adjust_table_values_loop
description: Repeatedly takes the absolute difference between two neighbouring table entries, scales it and adds it to a destination byte while scanning backward for flagged entries. When the scan ends it applies a final scaled correction to the flagged entries.

name: compute_scaled_envelope_tables
description: Walks flagged entries backward from the marked start, computing two scaled output values per entry from the stored level, with a rounded correction when a flag bit is set. It finishes by copying the last value to the output with a fixed offset.

name: apply_scaled_correction_pass
description: Walks flagged entries backward applying rounded, scaled corrections to two output tables, reloads the start offset from the flag table, and finishes by copying the last value with an offset.

name: compute_scaled_char_values
description: Loops backward over flagged entries computing scaled character values from two tables with multiplication and shifts, writes them to two destination tables, and at the end copies a byte and offsets it.

name: apply_pairwise_flag_corrections
description: For each run between two flagged entries, applies corrections whose multiplier depends on the distance between the flags, then makes a final pass that offsets flagged entries carrying a set bit.

name: apply_flag_pair_corrections
description: Applies the same distance-dependent corrections as its neighbour while scanning backward through the flagged entries, then runs the final offset pass over flagged entries.

name: apply_flag_run_corrections
description: Propagates corrections between flagged entries using a slope-based step, then writes the final flagged-entry values from the stored table and returns at the start of the table.

name: apply_flag_run_offsets
description: Applies the slope-based corrections for each flagged run, then runs the final offset pass over flagged entries that carry a set bit, returning at the start of the table.

name: apply_flag_run_slope_pass
description: Applies slope-based corrections to pairs of entries across each flagged run, stepping backward through the table and writing the flagged-entry offsets from the stored table once the start is reached.

name: apply_flag_run_slope_sweep
description: Repeats the slope-based run corrections over successive flagged entries, carrying the shift between runs, and returns after the final offset pass over flagged entries.

name: apply_flag_run_slope_reverse
description: Walks the flag table in reverse applying distance-dependent slope corrections to each flagged run, then writes the carried residual into the output and stops when its value is exhausted.

name: apply_flag_run_slope_loop
description: Applies the slope-based corrections across flagged runs with a repeating outer loop, adjusting the entries at each run boundary and ending with the offset pass over flagged entries.

name: apply_flag_run_slope_block
description: Applies the slope-based corrections across a block of flagged entries, using a per-entry multiplier chosen from the run length, and returns when the flag table is exhausted. It calls one helper routine.

name: apply_flag_run_slope_chain
description: Chains slope-based corrections along consecutive flagged entries, updating the two neighbouring tables at each step, and writes the final offsets for flagged entries before returning. It calls one helper routine.

name: apply_flag_run_slope_stage
description: Runs one stage of the slope-based correction over flagged runs, with the step size set by the run length, and writes the final offsets once the table is exhausted. It calls one helper routine.

name: apply_flag_run_slope_entry
description: Entry point for the slope-based run correction, which sets the initial step from the first entry and then loops over flagged runs writing offsets until the table ends. It calls three helper routines.

name: emit_running_max_offsets
description: Computes a scaled offset from the running maximum of the table values up to the current index and writes it to the output, then walks backward writing offsets for flagged entries and returns at the start. It calls one helper routine.

name: emit_running_max_offsets_alt
description: Performs the same running-maximum offset pass as its neighbour, taking its starting value from a register rather than a state field, and returns at the start of the table. It calls one helper routine.

name: emit_running_max_offsets_loop
description: Repeats the running-maximum offset computation across the table, writing a scaled value for each flagged entry, and returns at the start. It calls one helper routine.

name: scale_nibble_flagged_entries
description: Walks the table backward and, for each entry whose upper nibble is set, adds a sign-dependent scaled step from a second table to the entry, returning when the index reaches the start.

name: scale_nibble_flagged_entries_loop
description: Repeats the nibble-flag scaling over table entries from the current index downward, applying the same signed step, and returns at the start of the table. It calls one helper routine.

name: scale_buffer_by_signed_factor
description: Walks a byte range backward, skipping entries whose upper nibble is zero, and multiplies each remaining destination byte by a signed factor chosen from the source byte's sign to update the running value, repeating until the start is reached. It calls one helper routine.

name: distribute_run_differences_pass
description: Computes per-entry differences from three stored level tables, then walks flagged runs spreading each run's difference across its entries in halving steps, and finishes by filling the trailing run with fixed levels. It calls three helper routines.

name: spread_run_difference_steps
description: Repeats a backward copy-and-step over a run, then finds the next flagged run, spreads its difference evenly across the entries, and fills the trailing segment with fixed levels. It calls one helper routine.

name: spread_run_difference_variant
description: Spreads the difference of each flagged run across its entries using a count-based divisor, writing the adjusted levels and a final fixed-level fill for the trailing segment. It calls four helper routines.

name: spread_run_difference_stepper
description: Steps through flagged runs spreading each run's difference across its entries with a count-based divisor, and fills the trailing segment with fixed levels. It calls one helper routine.

name: spread_run_difference_entry
description: Entry point for spreading run differences: it makes one helper call, then walks flagged runs spreading each difference across its entries, and fills the trailing segment with fixed levels once the table ends. It calls three helper routines.

name: spread_run_difference_relay
description: Continues the run-difference spreading for the next flagged run, calling a helper on entry and branching to a separate path for two-entry runs, then fills the trailing segment with fixed levels. It calls two helper routines.

name: fill_trailing_segment_levels
description: Sets every entry to a fixed level, scales the flagged entries by their nibble, then spreads the final run's difference across its entries and writes the trailing fixed levels. It calls one helper routine.

name: fill_segment_levels_from_nibbles
description: Writes a fixed base level into each table entry and adds twice the entry's nibble, then spreads the trailing run's difference and fills its entries with fixed levels. It calls two helper routines.

name: spread_segment_difference_tail
description: Finds the start of the current flagged run, spreads its difference across the run in halving steps, and finishes by writing either the fixed level or the alternate level chosen by a mode byte. It calls one helper routine.

name: copy_and_offset_segment_levels
description: Copies each table entry one step forward with a fixed offset from the running value, then writes the final fixed level or the alternate one chosen by a mode byte. It calls two helper routines.

name: emit_running_max_offset_tail
description: Finds the largest value in the table below the current index, writes it as a scaled offset into the output and clears the matching flag byte, then copies the previous output entry when there is more than one entry.

name: accumulate_bytes_and_write_results
description: Scans table bytes backward keeping their running maximum, then writes a scaled value of that maximum and a derived copy into the output buffers, clearing the matching flag entry before returning.

name: apply_flag_class_steps
description: Walks flagged entries backward, applying sign-dependent scaled steps to the level and output tables according to each entry's class code, and returns when the start of the table is reached. It calls one helper routine.

name: apply_flag_class_steps_loop
description: Repeats the flagged-entry class stepping from the current index down to the start, updating the level and output tables for each flagged entry. It calls four helper routines.

name: apply_flag_class_steps_tail
description: Applies the initial class step to the entry at the current index, then loops over later entries in the flagged run, writing scaled steps until the start of the table. It calls one helper routine.

name: apply_flag_class_steps_entry
description: Entry point for flagged-entry class stepping, which applies an offset to the current entry and then repeats the class-based steps down through the table. It calls one helper routine.

name: apply_flag_class_steps_run
description: Applies the class-based steps across flagged runs, writing a scaled value for each entry and branching to a fixed-level fill for the trailing entry. It calls three helper routines.

name: apply_flag_class_steps_pair
description: Applies the class-based steps to pairs of entries with a fixed scale, then continues through the flagged table until the start is reached. It calls two helper routines.

name: apply_flag_class_steps_fixed
description: Applies a fixed-scale class step to each flagged entry while walking backward, and returns at the start of the table. It calls one helper routine.

name: apply_flag_class_steps_default
description: Applies a fixed-scale class step to the current entry, then loops backward through the flagged entries and returns at the start. It calls one helper routine.

name: apply_flag_class_steps_offset
description: Walks backward over the table applying the class-based steps and a signed offset to the output buffers, and returns once the start is reached. It calls one helper routine.

name: step_feedback_across_bytes
description: Repeats a feedback step across a byte range, copying each byte forward one place, scaling the running feedback by a table entry, subtracting it from the byte and writing the result to the output. It returns when the count is exhausted.

name: copy_adjust_bytes_with_feedback
description: Copies bytes between two buffers while updating a feedback value by multiplying it with a table entry and shifting, subtracts the feedback from each byte, and writes the adjusted bytes to two output areas. It returns when the count is exhausted.

name: check_narrator_flag_and_dispatch
description: Makes a fixed sequence of helper calls, then makes one more call only when a flag byte in the device state is non-zero. It does not modify memory or return a value.

name: run_three_helper_steps
description: Calls the same helper routine three times in succession and then returns, with no other work in between.

name: interpolate_and_store_bytes
description: Reads the first byte and the byte at the given index, then interpolates between them across eight-byte steps, storing the rounded result into the buffer at each step.

name: skip_group_markers_until_end
description: Scans a table in steps of eight bytes, skipping entries marked with the skip value and returning at the end marker, and calls a helper when a group is not the first.

name: skip_group_markers_by_count
description: Walks a sequence of eight-byte groups, advancing the pointer over each group and calling a helper for groups that are not full, until the end marker is reached.

name: skip_group_markers_then_scan
description: Calls a helper, then scans eight-byte groups for the end marker or the skip marker, advancing over each group and returning when the end marker is found.

name: scan_groups_until_end_marker
description: Scans eight-byte groups for the end marker, advancing the pointer over groups that are not the first and calling a helper for the first group that is not empty. It returns at the end marker.

name: advance_group_pointer_loop
description: Repeatedly advances through eight-byte groups, calling a helper when the group offset is not a full group, until the end marker is found. It returns after the end marker.

name: advance_group_pointer_scan
description: Calls a helper, then scans eight-byte groups for the end marker, advancing over full groups and returning when the end marker is reached.

name: write_character_rows_from_table
description: Walks a character list and its count list, writing either a block of column offsets or five-row glyph patterns from a table into the output for each character, with special handling for three characters. It returns at the terminator.

name: write_character_rows_with_stride
description: Processes the same character and count lists as its neighbour, writing five-row glyph patterns with a configurable stride or count-based offsets until the terminator. It calls three helper routines.

name: write_character_rows_loop
description: Repeats the character-row writing across the run lists, advancing the output by a count-derived step before each character, and returns at the terminator. It calls one helper routine.

name: write_character_rows_block
description: Writes a block of glyph rows for a count derived from the input, then continues through the character list with count-based offsets until the terminator. It calls two helper routines.

name: write_character_rows_mark
description: Writes glyph rows for a selected character, with a second special case for one more character, and continues through the list with count-based offsets until the terminator. It calls two helper routines.

name: write_character_rows_pair
description: Writes glyph rows for one special character and the default glyph, then continues through the list until the terminator. It calls one helper routine.

name: write_character_rows_triple
description: Writes glyph rows for three special characters and the default glyph, then continues through the character list until the terminator. It calls one helper routine.

name: apply_nibble_masks_to_rows
description: Walks the code list and, for entries flagged in the second table with more than two rows, halves and redistributes the nibble values across the row bytes, setting marker bytes at the row boundaries. It calls one helper routine.

name: apply_nibble_masks_rows_loop
description: Repeats the nibble redistribution across the code list, copying three-byte rows for the first two code values and clearing marker bytes at the row boundaries. It calls one helper routine.

name: apply_nibble_masks_by_flags
description: Applies the same nibble redistribution to each flagged code, using a bit mask from a separate flag word, and copies three-byte rows for the first two code values. It calls two helper routines.

name: apply_nibble_masks_by_run
description: Walks the code list applying nibble redistribution to each run of flagged codes, copies three-byte rows for the first two code values, and stops at the terminator. It calls two helper routines.

name: apply_nibble_masks_tail
description: Continues the nibble redistribution over the remaining codes, writing the boundary markers, until the terminator. It calls one helper routine.

name: remap_row_bytes_through_table
description: Walks eight-byte rows until the terminator, skipping rows marked with a special value, and replaces the three leading bytes of each other row with values looked up in a global table.

name: remap_row_bytes_forward
description: Writes three bytes from a lookup table into each row, stepping forward in eight-byte steps and returning when the row marker value appears.

name: stub_return_without_work
description: Contains only a return and performs no work, so calling it has no effect on the state.

name: sum_row_values_into_column
description: Sums the first byte of each six-entry row until a marker is reached, shifts the total right by three bits, and stores it into a fixed position at the end of each row.

name: accumulate_weighted_row_sums
description: Accumulates weighted values across six-entry rows, storing a shifted running total into a fixed position at the end of each row until the terminator is reached.

name: compute_row_weighted_average
description: Accumulates a weighted sum across each row's entries until the marker, then stores a scaled average into a fixed position of the row, repeating for each row.

name: compute_row_average_loop
description: Repeats the weighted row accumulation over successive rows, storing a scaled average into each row until the marker value is reached. It calls one helper routine.

name: emit_row_tail_values
description: Walks the code and count lists writing a fixed step value or a shifted offset into each row's tail for each code, with special cases for two codes and a marker code, until the terminator. It calls one helper routine.

name: emit_row_tail_values_stream
description: Processes the code and count lists in the same way as its neighbour, writing row-tail values for each code until the terminator. It calls several helper routines.

name: emit_row_tail_values_scan
description: Repeats the row-tail writing over the code and count lists, adding a fixed step for two special codes, and returns at the terminator. It calls one helper routine.

name: emit_row_tail_values_alt
description: Writes row-tail offsets for each code, using a negative fixed step for the default code, until the terminator. It calls one helper routine.

name: emit_row_tail_values_fast
description: Writes row-tail offsets using the default step and shifted offsets for other codes, returning at the terminator. It calls one helper routine.

name: emit_row_tail_values_pair
description: Writes row-tail offsets for pairs of codes with the same step rules as its neighbours, returning at the terminator. It calls one helper routine.

name: emit_row_tail_values_fill
description: Fills a row tail with a fixed value for each entry, then continues through the code list adding step values until the terminator. It calls one helper routine.

name: emit_row_tail_values_block
description: Adds shifted offsets for each entry in the row and writes the default fill for special codes, until the terminator. It calls one helper routine.

name: decode_nibble_checksum_bytes
description: Makes two passes over groups of five bytes, summing the low nibbles and then the high nibbles, and writes the combined checksum nibble back into the third byte of each group.

name: allocate_signal_and_wait
description: Stores the results of the exec library's signal allocation and task lookup in the device structure, then loops on the library wait call, calling a helper on each pass.

name: dequeue_request_and_dispatch
description: Takes the next node from a library list while the request flag is clear, records it in the device state unless its type is two, sets the in-progress bit and calls a helper, clearing the flags and returning when the list is empty.

name: clear_request_status_bits
description: Clears two status bits in the request block and returns.

name: start_speech_io_request
description: Fills the channel pointer table and the speech request block, configures the timing and buffer fields, writes the DMA control register, and sends the request through the exec I/O call.

name: render_speech_samples_double_buffered
description: Copies blocks of sample bytes from a source table, then generates each output sample by summing three lookup-table reads at advancing phase positions, filling one of two alternating audio buffers and switching buffers when a segment completes. It writes the DMA control register and calls helpers at buffer boundaries.

name: render_speech_samples_mixed
description: Mixes three table lookups per sample at advancing phase positions, or steps a counter that reflects at its bounds when a voice flag is set, writing sample pairs into the alternating audio buffers. It writes the DMA control register and calls several helpers at buffer boundaries.

name: render_speech_samples_looped
description: Advances the phase accumulators and fills the alternating audio buffers with summed table samples, returning when the source list ends and writing the DMA control register. It calls two helper routines.

name: render_speech_samples_pairs
description: Generates sample pairs for each code from the lookup tables and a voice counter, writing them into the alternating buffers and switching buffers at segment ends. It calls one helper routine.

name: render_speech_samples_tail
description: Writes mixed table samples into the active buffer for each segment, using a counter that reflects at its bounds, and finishes by writing the DMA control register. It calls four helper routines.

name: render_speech_samples_stepped
description: Steps a reflecting counter and writes summed table samples into the active buffer, looping over the source list until the terminator, then returns. It calls two helper routines.

name: render_speech_samples_wrapped
description: Repeats the sample generation over the source list, switching buffers and reflecting the counter at its bounds, and writes the DMA control register before returning. It calls two helper routines.

name: wait_io_and_enable_dma
description: Calls the library's wait-for-I/O routine once for each buffer in the speech request block, and writes the DMA control register to enable channels when a flag is set before returning.

name: enable_dma_if_flag_set
description: Writes the DMA control register to enable the DMA channels when a flag bit in the device state is set, then returns.

name: update_speech_request_interrupts
description: Sets the interrupt enable register to its enable value, increments a request counter, and when a new request byte differs from the stored one, links the matching request block and dispatches it through a library call. It restores the interrupt state when the counter drops.

name: decrement_counter_and_enable_interrupts
description: Decrements a counter in the device state and, when it was zero or one before the decrement, writes the interrupt enable value with its enable bit set.

name: flush_speech_buffer_chain
description: Marks each buffer in the chain as pending and calls its library handler, then either waits on the buffers or restarts the request through the I/O call, depending on a flag. It calls one helper routine.

name: flush_speech_buffer_range
description: Handles a range of buffers the same way as its neighbour, marking each pending and calling the library handler, then waits for them or restarts the request. It calls one helper routine.

name: wait_for_speech_buffers
description: Writes the DMA control register to enable channels when a flag is set, then calls the library wait routine for each buffer until one reports completion, marking the request as finished. It calls one helper routine.

name: mark_speech_request_done
description: Sets the done bit in the request status byte and returns.

name: load_hunk_executable_program
description: Opens the DOS library and allocates memory for the hunk table, then parses the executable's hunk headers and relocation records, reporting unsupported hunk types and out-of-memory errors before running the loaded program.

name: read_next_stream_byte
description: Reads the next byte from the input stream into the current-value variable and advances the stream pointer by one.

name: allocate_hunk_memory_block
description: Allocates a memory block for the current hunk and records it in the block table. On failure it sets the error state, releases earlier allocations and returns zero.

name: close_library_and_permit
description: Closes the DOS library handle when it is open, then calls the permit routine and returns zero.

name: free_hunk_buffers
description: Frees the hunk table and the relocation table, each only when it was allocated.

name: write_nul_terminated_message
description: Counts the characters of a NUL-terminated message and passes the message to two library output calls, returning afterwards.

name: decode_packed_stream_backwards
description: Unpacks a compressed stream from its end toward its start, reading bits through the refill routine and copying runs of earlier output. On its error path it writes a sequence of values to the background colour register before stopping.

name: output_bits_to_color_register
description: Writes successive bits from a packed value to the background colour register, refilling the value from the input when it runs out, for the requested number of steps.

name: program_entry_trampoline
description: Program entry point of the second file. The decompiler produced no body, so its only evidence is six instructions and a single call to another routine.

name: copy_handler_to_buffer
description: Allocates a memory block and, when allocation succeeds, copies a fixed-size code block into it and records the block address in a global variable, returning zero.

name: store_constants_to_stack
description: Writes two fixed 16-bit values into the stack frame and copies one global variable into another before returning.

name: initialize_system_and_dispatch
description: Stores a register value, obtains a base address and task data through library calls, runs setup helpers and a sequence of helper calls, then passes the resulting value to a library call. It uses the exec library's task and message-port calls.

name: stub_return_only
description: Consists only of a return instruction and does nothing.

name: dispatch_with_flags
description: Saves its input value into the state block, calls two table functions, then calls two more when a flag is set, and returns the saved value.

name: scan_hunk_list_until_end
description: Opens the library handles it needs, then scans hunk records until the end-of-hunk marker, closes the handles it opened and returns the last call result.

name: clear_flags_and_invoke
description: Clears a status flag, then for each of two pointer flags that are set, calls the matching library routine and clears that flag.

name: open_libraries_conditionally
description: Opens two system libraries, the second only when the first open succeeded, and returns the library handle or a fallback value.

name: close_libraries_conditionally
description: Closes each open library handle and clears its stored pointer, with the second close guarded by the outcome of the first.

name: handle_hunk_record_type
description: Branches on the hunk record type code, handling header, code and relocation records by calling helper routines, and returns for unknown types. It calls six helper routines.

name: open_library_loop
description: Repeatedly fetches a name and a length from a list, writes a terminating zero byte after the name, and calls the library open routine for each entry until the list ends.

name: build_allocated_entry_table
description: Allocates an entry list through the library call, then fills a table with entry records whose type codes are chosen from the top two bits of each value, and returns the allocated list or a clamped value.

name: compute_entry_range
description: Calls helper routines four times to obtain four values, then stores the difference between the last two, plus one, as the entry range.

name: process_table_with_crc
description: Runs a checksum over a table of long words, applying a shift-and-subtract mixing step to each non-zero entry, then compares the result with a value from another routine and returns it, or an all-ones value when they differ.

name: repeat_call_count_times
description: Calls a helper routine once for each unit of the input count, decrementing the count until it reaches zero.

name: return_global_flag
description: Calls a helper routine and then returns the value of a global flag.

name: invoke_library_function_conditionally
description: If the input value is non-zero, calls a library function through a pointer taken from a global variable, then returns.

name: initialize_and_process_loop
description: Calls setup helpers, then runs a four-iteration loop that calls helpers on each pass and, on the first pass, applies a trap and a bitwise XOR update to a byte, before a final helper call.

name: loop_with_early_exit
description: Calls two helper routines per iteration for a fixed number of iterations, returning early when the flag value is clear.

name: wait_for_nonzero_flag
description: Repeatedly calls a helper routine until the low seven bits of its result are non-zero and not greater than 79.

name: request_value_or_default
description: Calls a helper routine through a table pointer and returns its result, or the default value of 65536 when that result is zero.

name: allocate_memory_for_table
description: Calls the library's memory-allocation routine through a table pointer and returns its result, substituting the default size of 65536 when the result is zero.

name: free_block_if_valid
description: Frees a memory block through the library routine when the size value is non-zero and the pointer is set.

name: free_memory_conditionally
description: Calls the library free-memory routine through a pointer when both of its two inputs are non-zero.

name: compute_crc_checksum
description: Runs a bitwise CRC-16 over a byte buffer of the given length and returns the accumulated checksum combined with the input value.

name: increment_counter_and_return
description: Initialises a counter through a library call when it is zero, derives a new counter value from a helper call with a fixed seed, stores it incremented by one, and returns it.

name: compute_fixed_point_product
description: Multiplies two signed inputs as fixed-point values by combining the low-word product with cross terms, and returns the result negated when the signs differ.

name: wait_for_flag_match
description: Sets a global value and loops a fixed number of times calling helper routines; when a flag is set it compares two returned values and returns zero on a mismatch, or all ones when the loop finishes.

name: call_helper_once_then_return
description: Calls a helper routine and returns; its loop body runs only once because the loop flag is cleared before the call.

name: rotate_bits_with_condition
description: Obtains a word from a helper call and, when the zero flag is set, rotates its bits eight times through a carry, returning the resulting word.

name: wait_for_disk_sync_word
description: Repeatedly calls a helper routine until it returns the disk sync marker value, advancing a counter and looping when it wraps, and returns once the marker has been found.

name: scan_until_byte_matches
description: Calls a helper routine repeatedly, advancing a counter by a fixed step on each pass, until the returned byte equals the target byte or the counter reaches zero.

name: decode_mfm_pairs_until_marker
description: Reads pairs of values from a helper, combines the alternate bits of each pair with shifts and masks, and returns the decoded long word once its top byte is all ones.

name: call_helper_if_zero_result
description: Calls a helper routine and, when the zero flag is set, calls a second helper; the return path depends on whether the first result was zero.

name: read_bitfield_to_word
description: Returns a constant when a global counter has reached its limit; otherwise reads sixteen bits from a bit table, starting at the position given by the input, and returns them as a word.

name: open_resource_and_wait
description: Opens the disk resource, builds a message block with its fields set, then loops on the library wait and get-message calls until a non-zero value is returned.

name: invoke_cleanup_sequence
description: Runs a sequence of cleanup steps: it conditionally calls a library routine, frees a signal through the exec library, calls a further library routine, then returns after two helper calls.

name: initialize_message_structure
description: Calls a library routine for a signal number and, when the number is valid, allocates a message block and fills in its name, type, signal and list fields for the disk request port.

name: configure_custom_hardware
description: Writes the disk pointer, the disk control and DMA registers and the interrupt request register, then calls helper routines and returns a combined value.

name: configure_custom_registers
description: Waits while a status bit in the device state is set, then writes the disk pointer, control and DMA registers and calls helper routines before returning a combined value.

name: check_flag_and_set_values
description: Polls a flag word in the structure for up to 400000 iterations; when the flag is set it writes two values into fixed fields and returns zero, otherwise it returns all ones.

name: call_three_helpers_in_order
description: Calls three helper routines in sequence and returns, with no other work.
